variant: Championship robot, with the second ground intake; the catalog describes the earlier one

s7.title: 2231 OnyxTronix | Behind the Bumpers | 2025 FRC REEFSCAPE Robot

bet.text: Hold a coral and an algae at the same time and control both with the same system, so no cycle time is wasted.

demand.text: They saw at the start that the game rewards acceleration over top speed, and that scoring leaves about 5 cm of range, which a person cannot hit alone every time, so every action should be automated.
Wanted capabilities were ranked with QFD during about two days of game analysis.

cycle.text: The driver moves to an area such as a reef side and AutoPilot finishes the intake or score. The robot takes an algae off the reef and can place its coral immediately after. The end effector's rotation saves driving time between feeder and reef. An operator sets the scoring height.

endgame.text: A 'leg' locked by hooks holds the deep cage in place, and a passive 'beak' clamps onto it with the robot's weight. The catalog gives 1.0 second until the robot is in the air.

gave_up.text: A smaller drive pinion gives up maximum velocity for acceleration.

changed.text: The first algae ground intake, a roller held and driven from one side to save space, lacked performance and consistency at the Israeli events. A lightweight, compact and fast one came to the championship, with side wheels added to the algae mechanism. Both end effector sides were heavily modified.
At ISR 4 logs exposed an odometry problem and cameras were replaced.

outcome.text: 46-18-2 in official play; finalist in the Archimedes division; ranked 13 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 104.17, Archimedes).
